walkthroughs.h2: c = f × λ for EM waves
walkthroughs.body_html:
Every EM wave obeys c = f × λ, where c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

So if you know the frequency, you can work out the wavelength — and vice versa.

Example: visible light at f = 6 × 10¹⁴ Hz has λ = c / f = (3 × 10⁸) / (6 × 10¹⁴) = 5 × 10⁻⁷ m. That's green light. 💚

Because c is fixed, frequency and wavelength are inversely linked. If one goes up, the other must go down.

Radio: long wavelength, low frequency.
Gamma: short wavelength, very high frequency.

So if you're told a wave has the highest frequency in the spectrum, you instantly know it has the shortest wavelength too.

Use standard form when numbers get scary. 3 × 10⁸ means 300,000,000. 10⁻⁷ means 0.0000001.

When you divide, subtract the powers. (3 × 10⁸) ÷ (6 × 10¹⁴) = 0.5 × 10⁻⁶ = 5 × 10⁻⁷.

Always include units: wavelength in m, frequency in Hz, speed in m/s. ✅
